People do not need to be scared or to laugh, yet they buy tickets for both. Psychologists describe horror as a way to feel fear safely: the heart races, the danger is not real, and the relief afterward feels good. Comedy works in the opposite direction, releasing tension and helping people cope with stress.

This site looks at those two genres through what audiences actually did with their money. Out of about 3,300 movies, the typical horror film earned about 2.7 times its budget, the most of any genre, while the typical comedy earned about 1.9 times its budget. Choose your next showing:
